title: Robust State‐of‐Charge Estimation for Lithium‐Ion Batteries Using an Adaptive Invariant Extended Kalman Filter With an Enhanced Self‐Correcting Model
abstract: ABSTRACT State‐of‐Charge (SoC) estimation plays a vital role in the safe operation of lithium‐ion batteries, which can be used in different applications such as Electric Vehicles (EVs). However, traditional SoC estimation methods, such as Coulomb counting and Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), are often prone to accumulating errors, parameter uncertainty, and measurement noise under dynamic operating conditions. Therefore, in this work, an Adaptive Invariant Extended Kalman Filter (Adaptive IEKF) together with an Enhanced Self‐Correcting (ESC) battery model will be proposed to estimate SoC in real time. Parameters of the ESC model were found by means of OCV‐SoC characterization, Static Capacity Test (SCT), and Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization (HPPC). Measurement noise covariance adaptation on the basis of the innovation approach was used in order to increase robustness to uncertainty and variations in operating conditions. The developed algorithm was tested with the help of MATLAB/Simulink in the case of SCT and HPPC operating profiles and implemented on an STM32F446RE microcontroller in order to verify its performance under real‐time embedded conditions. The obtained experimental results confirm that the proposed technique keeps SoC estimation error under 2% under both dynamic and static operating conditions. During the HPPC, the Adaptive IEKF showed RMSE and MAE equal to 0.01487 and 0.0156, respectively, while for the SCT conditions, RMSE and MAE are 0.01112 and 0.01271, respectively.
title_zh: Robust State‐of‐Charge Estimation for Lithium‐Ion Batteries Using an Adaptive Invariant Extended Kalman Filter With an Enhanced Self‐Correcting Model

title: Advanced MPC-Based Bidirectional Equalization for Energy Balancing in Series-Connected EV Battery Cells
abstract: Cell imbalance in series-connected battery packs, typically caused by repeated charge–discharge cycles, negatively impacts capacity, lifespan, and safety in electric vehicle (EV) applications. To address these issues, effective and reliable cell balancing is critical for maintaining battery performance and ensuring consistent energy delivery. Conventional balancing approaches often face drawbacks such as inefficient charge redistribution, limited control of energy flow, and slower response. Although bidirectional equalization strategies reduce the risks of overcharging and overdischarging, challenges remain in achieving high balancing speed, superior energy efficiency, and reduced circuit complexity. This study introduces an active bidirectional cell-to-cell equalization strategy based on a multi-winding transformer topology, where energy is directly transferred from higher-voltage to lower-voltage cells through flyback operation. A time-sharing control algorithm guided by initial state-of-charge (SoC) optimizes the sequence and prevents unnecessary transfers, while an advanced Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme further enhances dynamic regulation, efficiency, and robustness of the balancing process. The proposed system is validated using MATLAB/Simulink 2019b and real-time hardware-in-the-loop testing with the OPAL-RT OP5700 platform, demonstrating superior equalization speed and energy utilization compared to conventional techniques.
title_zh: Advanced MPC-Based Bidirectional Equalization for Energy Balancing in Series-Connected EV Battery Cells

title: Electric vehicle battery fault detection and diagnosis agent: Descriptive text modeling of battery digital signals
abstract: With the rapid proliferation of electric vehicles, the safety and reliability of lithium-ion batteries have become critical concerns. Effective anomaly detection is essential for ensuring safe battery operation. However, as battery systems and operating scenarios become increasingly complex, Battery fault diagnosis and maintenance increasingly require stronger adaptability to heterogeneous operating scenarios and intelligent human–AI collaboration. Traditional fault detection and diagnosis paradigms are usually tailored to specific scenarios and predefined workflows, making them less effective in complex real-world applications. To address the scarcity of open-source battery fault report corpora and the lack of unified maintenance knowledge representation, this study investigates a descriptive text modeling approach for battery signal reports. Monitoring signals, statistical features, anomaly records, and state assessment results are transformed into structured and readable natural language descriptions, thereby constructing a language corpus for battery health diagnosis and maintenance. Based on this framework, we propose VBFDD-Agent, a vehicle battery fault detection and diagnosis agent for automotive-grade battery systems. VBFDD-Agent integrates descriptive battery-state texts, historical case retrieval, local maintenance manuals, and large language model reasoning to generate structured diagnostic results and maintenance recommendations. Experimental results show that the proposed framework can accurately perform anomaly monitoring and provide flexible, efficient, and actionable maintenance suggestions. Expert evaluation further confirms the practical value of the generated recommendations.
title_zh: Electric vehicle battery fault detection and diagnosis agent: Descriptive text modeling of battery digital signals

title: A hybrid time–frequency and cross-variable interactive Mamba network for accurate state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: The state of charge (SOC) of lithium-ion batteries is a critical variable for energy management and safety control in battery management systems. However, under wide temperature ranges and highly dynamic operating conditions, voltage–current–temperature sequences are affected by nonlinear coupling, noise interference, and long-range dependencies. These factors pose substantial challenges for end-to-end SOC estimation, including the balance between local transients and global trends, limitations in long-sequence modeling, and insufficient cross-variable interaction modeling. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel end-to-end SOC estimation model, termed HCFE–TFGM–VIEM. Specifically, a Hierarchical Convolutional Feature Extraction (HCFE) module is employed to extract local dynamic features from battery operating sequences. A Time–Frequency Gated Mixer (TFGM) module is then introduced to jointly model the sequence time–frequency structure through time–frequency convolution fusion and a prior-gated mechanism, improving the model’s adaptability to periodic variations and noise perturbations. Finally, an improved Variable Interaction-Enhanced Mamba (VIEM) module is proposed to explicitly characterize the interactions among multiple variables such as voltage, current, and temperature. This module alleviates the insufficient variable interaction modeling caused by the channel-independent property of the Mamba architecture and enables stable long-range dependency modeling. Extensive experiments on the public LG 18650HG2 dataset under multiple temperatures ( − 20 ° C , − 10 ° C , 0 ° C , 10 ° C , 25 ° C , and 40 ° C ) and representative driving cycles demonstrate that the proposed model achieves favorable and consistent performance across the evaluated temperature and driving-cycle conditions within the LG 18650HG2 dataset. Under the 0 ° C condition, the average MAX, MAE, and RMSE are 2.65%, 0.40%, and 0.52%, respectively, achieving the best overall performance among the models evaluated under the common protocol and showing favorable numerical results compared with the results reported for representative advanced SOC estimation methods, while demonstrating accurate and robust SOC estimation under the evaluated conditions.
title_zh: A hybrid time–frequency and cross-variable interactive Mamba network for accurate state-of-charge estimation of lithium-ion batteries
